chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma'a, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! When the maid intends to prepare the food, instruct her to measure it, for indeed the blessing is in what is measured.'
ai.seo_question: Why is measuring food important in Shia Islam according to the hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual efficacy of food to the precision of measurement, emphasizing that *barakah* (divine blessing) is intrinsically tied to certainty and the avoidance of *gharar* (uncertainty). This teaching extends beyond mere culinary practice, serving as a microcosm for fair trade and honest household management, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating spiritual purity with practical daily conduct. The directive to 'measure' rather than estimate underscores the importance of tangible evidence in securing divine favor in mundane activities.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Abu Sayyar! Whenever you want the maid to make the food, so instruct her for measuring it, for the Blessings are in what is measured’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al- Rahman from Misma’ who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O abu Sayyar, when the female servant prepares food, ask her to measure; blessings come with measurement.’”
